indicators: Mismatch between email SPF pass and DKIM fail
Email originating IP 203.0.113.45 not recognized in trusted IP list for finance.cfo@legitcorp.com
Deepfake detection score > 0.9 on audio attachment
Unusual high-value wire transfer immediately after receiving deepfake audio
Email Message-ID timestamp does not align with normal CFO activity hours
example.detection_method: Deploy an AI-based deepfake audio detection system integrated with email gateway to scan audio attachments for synthetic voice artifacts. Implement DMARC policies with strict DKIM validation and alert on DKIM failures despite passing SPF. Monitor financial system logs for anomalous wire transfer requests triggered after receiving email with audio attachments. Correlate email source IP addresses with known trusted IPs for executives. Establish multi-factor verification (phone call or in-person) for wire transfers exceeding predefined thresholds.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1076 - Remote Services (for potential follow-up access)
T1485 - Data Destruction (if attacker deletes logs post-fraud)
T1566.002 - Phishing: Spearphishing Link (for related phishing campaigns)

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents the AI-enabled deepfake social engineering problem. The scenario clearly describes the use of AI-generated deepfake audio impersonating a trusted individual (the CFO) to manipulate a finance employee into transferring funds, aligning well with the problem nature. The technical data is comprehensive and realistic, including email content with an audio attachment, SMTP logs, DNS registration details, email header analysis showing SPF pass but DKIM fail, deepfake detection metadata with a high detection score, and financial system logs showing the suspicious wire transfer. Indicators are well articulated, explaining why the sample matches the problem, such as DKIM failure despite SPF pass, unrecognized originating IP, high deepfake detection score, and unusual financial activity. The detection method is detailed and appropriate, covering AI-based detection, email authentication policies, log monitoring, IP correlation, and multi-factor verification, which aligns with the recommended risk reduction strategies. Relevant MITRE techniques are correctly identified and relevant to the scenario. Overall, the sample is complete, realistic, and correctly aligned with the problem description.
